title: Protocol for isolating young adult parvalbumin interneurons from the mouse brain for extraction of high-quality RNA
protocol: Fill another bucket with ice.
Pour approximately 80 mL of the slushy cutting solution into a 100 mL storage bottle and place it in the ice bucket along with a tissue forceps, standard scissors, and micro-dissecting scissors.
Fill the custom-made or commercial incubation chamber with micro-dissecting solution and place it on ice next to the bubbling cutting solution.
Keep the cutting solution saturated using a solvent inlet bubbler line.
Place a double-edge razor blade in a 20 mm glass petri dish with acetone for 5 min.
Scrape residual glue off the blade and rinse with copious amount of water.
Mount the blade on the vibratome.
Set up optimal slicing settings for your machine.
Cut 350 μm-thick slices using an advancing speed of 0.1–0.15 mm/s and 1 mm amplitude to obtain healthy slices.
Move the ice bucket with the cutting solution containing syringe and 100 ml storage bottle as well as tools to the dissection area.
Remove the ice tray from the freezer and rinse the inner dish containing the Sylgard in order to dispose ice from accidental water spillage.
Add the slushy cold cutting solution from the 100 ml storage bottle to the Sylgard dish and bubble it with the inlet solvent diffuser in the dissection area.
Place the mouse in the induction chamber.
Turn on oxygen tank and vaporizer filled with isoflurane (1–2%).
Wait until limb and eye reflexes have disappeared.
Decapitate the animal using standard scissors.
Place the head in the slushy cutting solution in the ice tray.
Cut the skin longitudinally along the skull median line and laterally to fully expose the skull.
Cut the skull bone longitudinally along the median line, advancing from back to front with extreme care.
Make a last transverse cut along the nasal bone.
Use bone rongeurs to pull the skull top from the brain.
Gently scoop the brain using a long-curved tip spatula.
Cut out the cerebellum and olfactory bulbs while in the slushy bubbling solution.
Allow the brain to recover for 2–3 min in the ice tray while bubbling using the solvent inlet filter line.
Place a 42.5 mm round filter on the back of the glass petri dish.
Dampen the filter with cold cutting solution.
Gently place the brain on the soaked filter paper using a flat squared tip spatula.
Remove excess cutting solution using a transfer pipette or pieces of filter paper sequentially.
Apply a dab of glue on the surface of the specimen holder in front of the agar block.
Use a strip of filter paper to lift the brain from the back of the petri dish and place it on the glue.
Ensure the back of the brain is in contact with the agar block.
Place a 4% agar block on the specimen holder prior to mounting the brain.
Mount the brain between the agar block and the advancing blade holder.
Fill the stage chamber with ice-slushy cutting solution quickly after placing the specimen holder with the attached brain.
Set up a cutting window if your vibratome allows for it.
Remove the inlet solvent bubbler from the ice tray and place it in the stage chamber away from the cutting blade.
Cut the tip of a transfer pipette to create an opening large enough to capture slices as they come off the blade.
Cut 350 μm-thick transverse slices.
Carefully pick up each slice as they come off the blade using the wide mouth transfer pipette.
Place the slices inside the bubbling incubation chamber sitting on ice.
Move the slices to an ice tray with bubbling recovery solution for microdissection under a microscope immediately after collecting the last slice from the vibratome.
Adjust the optical settings on the dissection microscope.
Hold the brain slice gently with a sable brush.
Cut the cortex and hippocampus from subcortical brain structures of both hemispheres with a scalpel blade.
Mince tissue into small chunks and collect them in a 15 mL Falcon tube along with microdissection solution.
Remove microdissection solution from the 15 mL Falcon tube using a transfer pipette.
Add approximately 2.6 mL of EBSS#1-papain-DNase mixture to the Falcon tube.
Displace air in the vial with carbogen tubing at room temperature for 2–3 minutes without bubbling gas through the solution.
Cap the Falcon tube and seal it with parafilm, then wrap it in foil.
Tape the sealed and wrapped Falcon tube to a rocking platform in the hybridization oven/incubator.
Incubate the tube for approximately 90 minutes at 37°C.
Set a centrifuge for 15 mL tubes to room temperature (21°C–23°C) for short spins.
Precoat Eppendorf LoBind Microcentrifuge or 15 mL Falcon tubes with 30% BSA at room temperature (21°C–23°C).
Prepare EBSS#2 solution in a 50 mL Falcon tube: mix 9.6 mL EBSS, 700 μL OPI, and 500 μL DNAse 1, then add 1.2 cc of 50% Trehalose in EBSS for a total volume of 12 mL.
Place the prepared EBSS#2 solution on ice.
Prepare OPI discontinuous density gradient medium: mix 5 mL OPI in EBSS with 0.6 mL of 50% Trehalose in EBSS for a total volume of 5.6 mL per brain, then place it on ice.
Triturate the mixture 8–10 times using a 10 mL serological pipette over 30–40 minutes.
Let non-dissociated chunks settle for a couple of minutes and collect the cloudy suspension for centrifugation in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge the suspension at 300 g (∼1800 RPM) for 5 min at room temperature (21–23°C).
Discard the supernatant and gently re-suspend the pellet in 3 mL of mixed EBSS#2 solution by trituration with a 1 mL micropipette while avoiding air bubbles.
Slowly and gently layer the cell suspension onto the OPI discontinuous density gradient medium without agitating.
Centrifuge at 70 g (∼800 RPM) for 6 minutes at room temperature (21–23°C).
Discard the supernatant and re-suspend the pellet in 2 mL of FACS solution using a 1 mL micropipette.
Take 50 μL of cell suspension and add it to 250 μL of 0.4% trypan blue.
Mix well and mount on a hemocytometer.
Count the live, unstained cells in 4 corner squares on the hemocytometer.
Take the average cell count and multiply by 10,000 (1×10^4).
Multiply by five to correct for the 1:5 dilution from the trypan blue addition.
Aspirate BSA from 15 mL Falcon tubes or Eppendorf LoBind Microcentrifuge tubes and add the desired FACS collection solution.
Rinse flow cytometer tubing with one run of RNase free dH2O, then bleach followed by RNase free dH2O.
Set up the nozzle size to 100 μm with a sheath pressure of 45 psi.
Excite TdTomato using an argon-ion laser at 488 nm.
Detect TdTomato emission spectra between 564 nm and 606 nm.
Limit sorting time to 60-75 minutes per sample.
Conduct sorting at slow speed to prevent damage to neurons.
Take a few cells at the beginning of sorting for microscopic observation.
Ensure observed cells are well dissociated and viable.
Confirm that observed cells are Tomato red positive.
Use proper forward (FSC) and side scatter (SSC) properties to exclude debris and doublets.
Check the intensity of the fluorescence.
Adjust gating to ensure that only fluorescence positive cells are collected.
Set up a timer at the start of sorting.
Collect TdTomato+ cells in Eppendorf micro-centrifuge tubes or 15 mL Falcon tubes with FACS solution or TRIzol LS.
Limit collection volume to 250 μL if collecting directly in TRIzol LS.
Restrict total sorting time to 1–2 hours.
Spin the collected cells at 140 g (∼1300 RPM) for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Keep the cell pellet at -80°C until RNA preparation is needed.
Thaw your FACS sample on ice.
Add 1 mL of TRIzol LS while thawing if starting from a frozen pellet of FACS cells.
Homogenize the sample by intermittent vortexing for 2 min and then pipetting up and down (10×).
Incubate the homogenized sample at room temperature for 5 min to permit complete dissociation of the nucleoprotein complex.
Add 267 μL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol LS used for homogenization.
Cap the tube securely and shake vigorously by hand for 15 s.
Incubate the sample at room temperature (21°–23°) for 15 min.
Spin the centrifuge at 12,000 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Remove the aqueous phase by decanting into a clean new tube.
Add 2 μL of linear acrylamide to the aqueous phase and gently mix by inverting the tube.
Add 666 μL of 100% isopropanol per 1 mL TRIzol LS used for homogenization and gently mix by inverting the tube for 15 s.
Incubate at room temperature (21°–23°) for 10 min.
Spin at 12,000 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant without disturbing the RNA pellet.
Resuspend the RNA pellet in 100 μL of DEPC-treated water.
Add 200 μL of 100% ethanol to the resuspended RNA.
Add 10 μL of 3M sodium acetate to the solution.
Briefly vortex the mixture to mix well.
Store the mixture at -20°C for at least 1 hour.
Spin the sample at 14000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Wash the RNA pellet with 1 mL of 75% cold ethanol (prepared with DEPC-treated water) by gently inverting the tube.
Spin the sample at 14000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after washing.
Air dry the pellet for about 5 minutes to remove residual ethanol.
Resuspend the pellet in approximately 25 μL of DEPC-treated water.
Estimate the RNA yield using a nanodrop or fluorescent-based method (e.g., Qubit).
Store the RNA sample at -80°C until use for RNAseq or other experimental plans.
